symptom: The French TeX names ringed spaces (X,A) and (Y,B) but then writes the ψ-morphism as θ:G→F, although G and F are undefined in this environment.
cause_evidence: The surrounding pair notation, the composite θ''=ψ'_*(θ)∘θ', and the standard typing of a ringed-space morphism require θ:B→A as a ψ-morphism. The same G/F letters are generic variables in 3.5.1, suggesting an unreplaced carry-over rather than new objects.
attempted: Copy θ:G→F literally; rejected because it introduces undefined objects into the defining paragraph.
Normalize only the Korean target to the contextually typed θ:B→A while preserving the French authority unchanged.
resolution: Korean target uses θ:B→A and the discrepancy is durably recorded; French source remains read-only pending its owner's independent source adjudication.
tests: Cumulative XeLaTeX three-pass build succeeds, diagnostics0; PDF extraction and direct visual inspection of pages24-26 PASS.
residual_risk: The live French authority still contains G/F, so a later source correction may require a one-delta rebase even though the Korean mathematical typing is already B/A.
recurrence: When a definition reuses generic letters from a cited construction, verify typing against the named objects and composition law before translating.
